title: Identifiability: GPS coordinates reveal child's location and movements
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted from the child's device can be used to identify the child's precise location, movements, and patterns of behavior, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about their whereabouts and activities.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted with sufficient precision to identify specific locations; the data is not anonymized or aggregated before transmission.

title: Disclosure: Backend may expose GPS data to unauthorized parties
description: The Mobile App Backend process may store, log, or share GPS coordinate data with third parties, employees, or systems without proper authorization, leading to unauthorized access to the child's location information.
assumptions: The backend system has access controls that may not be properly implemented; data may be shared with analytics, marketing, or other third-party services.

title: Data Minimization: Excessive GPS collection at regular intervals
description: Collecting live GPS coordinates at regular intervals may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose, resulting in unnecessary tracking of the child's movements and accumulation of detailed location history.
assumptions: The stated purpose does not require continuous real-time location tracking; less frequent or less precise location data could suffice.

title: Explicit Location Data Disclosure to Storage
description: The backend process explicitly writes location pings to the Location History Store. This represents an intentional transfer of personal data (location information) across a system boundary. The minimality principle should be evaluated: is storing full location history strictly necessary, or could it be limited to aggregated/anonymized data?
assumptions: Location data is considered personal data under privacy regulations

title: Linkability of Location Data to Individuals
description: Location data stored in DS1 can potentially be linked to specific users, enabling tracking of movement patterns and correlating with other data sources to identify individuals.
assumptions: Location data is personally identifiable when combined with user identifiers

title: Identifiability Through Location History
description: Stored location pings can directly identify individuals by revealing their physical presence at specific times and places, potentially enabling profiling or surveillance.
assumptions: Location data alone or in combination with other data can identify individuals

title: Explicit Location Data Disclosure to Geofencing Engine
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) explicitly transfers location pings to Geofencing Engine (P2) for zone entry/exit checking. This represents an intentional data disclosure where personal location data crosses a process boundary.
assumptions: Location pings contain personal data that can identify or track individuals
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on Process→Process mapping context

title: Location Data Linking Risk
description: Location pings transferred from P1 to P2 can be linked with other data sources to create detailed movement profiles, potentially enabling identification of individuals through location patterns and temporal correlation.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with other datasets to identify individuals
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 node chosen based on Process→Process interaction context

title: Location Data Identification Risk
description: Location pings inherently contain identifying information about individuals' movements and whereabouts. The transfer to P2 for geofencing purposes creates identification risks if data is not properly protected or if geofencing results are exposed.
assumptions: Location data can identify individuals, especially when combined with timestamps
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 node chosen based on Process→Process interaction context

If accessed by unauthorized parties, this could reveal sensitive location patterns and personal information about family members.

title: Unauthorized access to zone configuration data

title: Linkability of zone data to other family data
